changes: p2: 'dasakhata' read as Hindi dastkhat 'handwriting/signature' (not part of the name); name kept as Guravakaśa, probably the Hindi name Gurbakhś (Gurubakhśa); confidence lowered to medium because the reading is not certain
p2: residence given as written (Kāśī) and normalized to Vārāṇasī in place
date: month normalized to Mārgaśīrṣa (agahana); paksa normalized to kṛṣṇa (badī); weekday to Saturday (śanaiścara)
notes: expanded on dastkhat, the pūrṇimānta month reckoning, and the unclear 'arīparaḥ cīraṃjīvīnāmaḥ'

notes: The colophon is in Hindi. 'mīti' is miti and 'līkhāḥ' is likhā. 'dasakhata' is dastkhat, 'handwriting/signature', so the phrase reads 'written in the hand of Guravakaśa (probably Gurbakhś) Kāyastha (kāetha), in Kāśī (kāsī madhye)'. The era is not named: 'saṃvat' with a Hindi date formula (agahana badī) points to Vikrama. Under the North Indian pūrṇimānta reckoning, Agahana badī 1 falls about late October or November 1767 CE. I did not verify the weekday. 'arīparaḥ cīraṃjīvīnāmaḥ' is unclear. It may name a locality in Kāśī (Haripura?) and a person Cirañjīvī, perhaps the owner or beneficiary. It may also be a corrupt blessing formula (cirañjīvī). Cirañjīvī is therefore recorded with role 'other' and low confidence.
